title: Quantized weight format compatibility breakage — remediation and rollout plan
creator: Asha Patel
summary: A change to the quantized weight serializer produced a different per-channel scale/zero-point ordering. This caused a subset of newly-uploaded quantized model bundles to be incorrectly interpreted by the runtime kernel selector, producing unsupported-op errors and crash loops in Dedicated hosts and accuracy regressions when falling back to float variants.
incident_description: On 2025-02-17 we started receiving alerts for multiple Dedicated pools reporting frequent model load failures and crash loops after a wave of model bundle uploads. Simultaneously, we observed elevated error rates and elevated tail latency for hosted generation endpoints that fell back to float model variants. The upstream change was a patch to the model exporter that re-ordered per-channel quantization metadata for storage compaction. Runtime deserializers expected the legacy ordering; a mismatch led to invalid kernel selection (unsupported ops) and incorrect dequant arithmetic resulting in deterministically bad outputs.
timeline_highlights:
2025-02-17 02:10 UTC - First alerts from Dedicated pool A (OOM/crash loop).
2025-02-17 02:22 UTC - SRE paged on elevated crashloop rate.
2025-02-17 03:05 UTC - Identified correlation with newly uploaded quantized bundles via registry audit.
2025-02-17 04:10 UTC - Rollback: blocked new model uploads to affected registry shard.
2025-02-17 07:30 UTC - Deploy emergency sanitizer in serving runtime to reject mismatched metadata.
2025-02-17 12:00 UTC - Temporary mitigation: automatic model requeue to safe float variants for impacted routes.
2025-02-18 09:00 UTC - Root cause confirmed: serializer ordering change in exporter v2.4.1.
2025-02-19 15:00 UTC - QA patch for deserializer compatibility landed behind feature gate
impact: Affected ~6 Dedicated pools across three regions; 12 internal services experienced retries and elevated latency. Several enterprise customers reported failed model rollouts during the incident window. Estimated served token loss due to degraded throughput: ~1.2M tokens. No data exposure was detected.
root_cause: A backwards-incompatible change to the quantized weight metadata ordering in the exporter produced bundles that the runtime deserializer misinterpreted. The kernel-selection logic treated the malformed metadata as indicating an unsupported per-channel layout and fell back to codepaths that were not robust for the combination of model architecture + quant format, leading to crash loops. Additionally, there was insufficient versioning metadata in model bundles to allow graceful negotiation of format differences.
immediate_actions_taken:
1) Blocked model uploads to the affected registry shard.
2) Hotfix sanitizer in runtime to detect and reject the malformed ordering (prevented crash loops).
3) Automated requeue of impacted endpoints to float variants to restore availability.
4) Reverted exporter binary patch in the CI pipeline and re-published a compatibility-tagged build.
5) Notified affected customers and provided rollback/playback instructions.
permanent_remediation_plan:
1) Add explicit format versioning to model bundle manifest and enforce at load time.
2) Implement a tolerant deserializer that accepts both legacy and new per-channel ordering patterns and normalizes into canonical internal representation.
3) Harden kernel-selection heuristics to validate metadata vs. actual tensor contents before choosing specialized kernels; fallback to safe reference kernels only after grace checks.
4) Add pre-upload CI checks in exporter to validate bundle roundtrip with the current runtime.
5) Build an automated registry scanner to detect any existing bundles that use the new ordering and either flag or convert them.

next_steps_and_timeline:
By 2025-02-28: land tolerant deserializer and versioned manifest.
By 2025-03-05: deploy kernel-selection validation + CI roundtrip tests.
By 2025-03-12: run registry scan, convert flagged bundles or notify owners.
By 2025-03-19: complete docs and rollout postmortem to customers and internal teams.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for legacy + new ordering deserialization.
- End-to-end roundtrip export->upload->serve tests on representative model zoo (transformer encoder/decoder and embedding-only models).
- Fuzz tests that mutate per-channel metadata and assert safe rejection or normalization.
- Load tests to ensure sanitizer prevents crash loops under high concurrent loads.
monitoring_and_alerting_changes:
- New metric: model_bundle_manifest_version_mismatch (counter).
- Alert: >1 rejected bundle per minute in a registry shard triggers P1.
- Dashboards: dedicated pool crashloop rate tied to model-load-failure reasons.
- Add synthetic canary that uploads a compatibility-tagged bundle and verifies runtime accepts it.
rollback_plan: If post-fix regressions appear in canaries, 1) block uploader traffic to problematic registry shard; 2) revert runtime change and re-enable sanitizer; 3) fallback impacted routes to float or verified quantized model variants; 4) open on-call bridge for rapid triage.
customer_communication_summary: We proactively contacted affected customers with incident timeline, recommended rollbacks, and mitigation steps. For enterprise accounts with Dedicated pools we offered assisted conversion of impacted bundles and prioritized conversion tickets. Draft for public postmortem and customer FAQ is in progress.
postmortem_notes: This incident exposed a fragile implicit contract between exporter and runtime. Versioning and explicit schema checks are low-effort, high-value controls. We should tighten our CI matrix to include cross-repo compatibility gates for any serialization changes. The sanitizer prevented broader customer impact and should be extended to other bundle metadata fields.
conclusion: Root cause identified and mitigations deployed; delivering compatibility and CI hardening across the next three sprints. Ownership assigned and customer remediation underway. The risk of similar regressions is reduced by planned manifest versioning and tolerant deserialization.
